videos.title: TSMC Employees Inspired by Samsung Strike? Calls for Walkout Over Bonus Cut Rumors (05/25/2026/Ne...
videos.subtitle_summary:
1. Samsung's strike is causing a ripple effect in Taiwan, with rumors circulating among TSMC employees that the company may cut their performance bonuses by 15%. This comes despite TSMC's record-breaking first quarter profit of approximately $26 billion.
2. TSMC employees are reportedly strongly opposing the potential bonus cut, citing the company's recent large-scale investments in building semiconductor factories in various countries, including the U.S. and Japan.
3. Local media in Taiwan have reported that Samsung union members are currently holding a vote on the distribution of performance bonuses, which has sparked concerns that TSMC may follow suit with its own strike.

videos.title: Made 26 Trillion Won, Yet Cutting Bonuses? TSMC Staff Say "Time to Strike" (05/26/2026/News Today...
videos.subtitle_summary:
1. TSMC, the world's leading semiconductor foundry, is experiencing the impact of Samsung's strike. Despite a significant increase in TSMC's first-quarter earnings this year, there are reports of plans to cut employee bonuses by 15%. This has sparked strong opposition among TSMC employees who question why they should work hard every day only to have their performance bonuses reduced.
2. The background for the proposed bonus cuts is TSMC's large-scale investment in building semiconductor factories in various countries, including the U.S. and Japan. Local media in Taiwan have reported that TSMC employees are planning a strike in response.
3. Meanwhile, reports suggest that Samsung's labor union in South Korea is conducting a vote on the distribution of performance bonuses. This has raised concerns in Taiwan, where some media outlets predict that a strike at TSMC could have a more significant impact than Samsung's strike.

videos.subtitle_summary:
1. Samsung affiliates are demanding bonuses following a large-scale agreement at Samsung Electronics, questioning whether they are second-tier to Samsung.
2. TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company) is also calling for performance-based wages similar to Samsung.
3. The demand for increased bonuses at Samsung, especially at Samsung Electrics, is causing unrest due to expectations of record profits this year. This issue is spreading globally.
